# Message List

## Concept

### Pitch

The chat history of prompt mode: the prompts sent to the harness and its responses, as a conversation.

### Shape

#### Description

Conversation-style, shows send prompts on the right, received input on the left.

#### Sent Prompt

A sent prompt shows the compiled markdown that was actually sent to the harness, rendered as markdown, once it has compiled. Its message header shows the name of the hidden anchor it was compiled from.

#### Response

A response from the harness is grouped by general type, in the order it happened. The harness's own text is shown as markdown. Tool calls in a row that share a general type (reading and searching files, editing files, running commands, the web, agents, and anything else) are gathered into one group, headed by that type and how many calls it holds. Each call in a group lists the tool's name, its most telling argument, and whether it is running, done, or failed, spelled out rather than only coloured.

#### Queue Background

The header along the top of the message list, holding the pinned prompt and the queue, has the same background colour as the tab bar.

#### Legibility

The output from a realtime agent should be readable and meaningful.  Make sure the font size is large enough, that the colours are legible.

name: build-application
description: build or change the ApplicationScope scope Use when you need to build or change the ApplicationScope scope
---

Read all necessary skills and specs, then build or change the ApplicationScope scope according to what already exists in the codebase.
If nothing has been built, start from scratch.
If you're not starting from scratch, analyze the existing codebase against the spec and determine what needs to be changed and/or refactored. It might be small changes or additions, or it might be a large refactor.  No matter the scale, make sure the spec acts as the source of truth and the code is reworked to match the spec.

# Refactoring

Always build from the latest spec, checking what's already build in [ApplicationScope](../../reference/scope/application/ApplicationScope.md) against the spec.  Spec is the source of truth, and the code should be refactored to match the spec.

# Belay Shape

Use the directory structure of ../../reference/shape to guide how to structure and organize the code.  If the shape changes, refactor the code to match.
Do not use the structure of the spec to fundamentally guide the layout of the application.  The only guidance you should look at for structure/organization is ../../reference/shape.

# Scope

## Concept

### Pitch

A REPL and sort of notebook for [Piton](https://piton-lang.org/spec.md) that allows you write prompts that references the spec and also allows you to build up a history of prompts saved as files.

### Shape

#### Description

desktop application

#### Stack

```
language: rust
gui: gpui
components: [gpui-kit](https://gpui-kit.com/)
```

#### Platforms

- windows
- mac
- linux

#### Main Window

[MainWindowScope](../../reference/scope/application/MainWindowScope.md)

Links in this document point at reference files. Read one when the work touches what it describes.

content.text:
The queued-prompts row now sits at the bottom of the message list, just above the chat input. The prompt the harness is working on stays pinned at the top.

**What changed** (all in `src/prompt_mode.rs`):
- **Split the header in two:** `render_header` now draws only the latest task. A new `render_queue` draws the "N queued" row with its chevron, the "Send next" button, the auto-send switch and the expanding list of queued prompts.
- **Placement:** the queue comes after the output (or after the task list, when the history is expanded). It keeps the tab-bar background and has a border on top instead of below. It still only shows while something is queued.
- **Test:** I renamed the queue UI test to `queue_is_below_the_output_and_can_be_cancelled`, and it now checks that the queued prompts are below the output.
